- Collaborate with developers, AI engineers, and automation specialists throughout the delivery lifecycle. 

- Design workflows incorporating: 

- Autonomous and semi-autonomous agents

- Human review and approval stages

- Escalation paths

- Exception handling

- Feedback loops

- Continuous learning mechanisms

- Drive adoption of reusable components, templates, skills, prompts, and accelerators across initiatives. 

- Support enterprise rollout, change management, and operational readiness activities. 

Stakeholder Management & Leadership

- Serve as the primary liaison between business stakeholders, delivery teams, and leadership. 

- Communicate solution vision, business value, risks, and implementation approaches to executive and technical audiences. 

- Manage competing priorities and navigate ambiguity in complex transformation programs. 

- Facilitate decision-making and proactively escalate risks, dependencies, and roadblocks. 

- Mentor team members and promote best practices in agentic automation delivery. 

Responsible AI, Governance & Risk Management

- Ensure all solutions comply with Pearson's Responsible AI framework. 

- Implement controls to mitigate: 

- Hallucination risks

- Prompt injection attacks

- Data leakage

- Model misuse

- Compliance and privacy risks

- Apply governance requirements based on solution risk levels including low, medium, and high-stakes use cases. 

- Support auditability, explainability, transparency, and regulatory compliance requirements. 

- Partner with security, legal, privacy, and risk teams to ensure enterprise readiness. 

Delivery Excellence & Business Impact

- Partner with program and project managers to ensure successful execution and delivery. 

- Define and track success metrics including: 

- Productivity improvements

- Cost reduction and avoidance

- Time savings

- Automation utilization

- Employee experience improvements

- Customer experience outcomes

- Ensure solutions integrate with enterprise observability, monitoring, telemetry, and governance platforms. 

- Drive continuous optimization through performance measurement and feedback. 

Innovation & Capability Building

- Contribute to Pearson's AgentOps roadmap and enterprise AI strategy. 

- Create and maintain reusable assets including: 

- Prompt libraries

- Agent templates

- Automation accelerators

- Design standards

- Playbooks and frameworks

- Evaluate emerging AI, agentic, and automation technologies. 

- Champion an agentic-first mindset and culture of continuous learning across the organization. 

Technology Ecosystem

Agentic AI & Large Language Models

- Azure OpenAI

- OpenAI APIs

- Claude

- Enterprise AI Platforms

- Multi-Agent Frameworks

Automation & Orchestration

- UiPath Studio

- UiPath Document Understanding

- Microsoft Power Automate

- Oracle

- OCR & Intelligent Document Processing

Engineering & Development

- Git & Version Control

- AI-Assisted Development Tools (Claude, Cursor, GitHub Copilot)

Required Qualifications

Education

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline. 

- Master's degree preferred but not required. 

Experience

- 8+ years of experience in technology consulting, digital transformation, automation, AI, or enterprise solution delivery. 

- Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional automation and AI initiatives. 

- Strong experience conducting discovery workshops and translating business requirements into technology solutions. 

- Proven success delivering measurable business outcomes through automation, AI, or enterprise transformation programs. 

Technical & Functional Expertise

Deep understanding of:

- AI governance and Responsible AI principles

Leadership Competencies

Success Measures

Success in this role will be measured by:

data.description:
Shape the Future of Connected Systems as a Software Engineer II (Trimble Unity)

Are you a highly skilled API Developer ready to build solutions for enterprise applications? As a P2-level Software Engineer, you will bring hands-on expertise to design, develop, and integrate scalable, secure RESTful services. You will work closely with cross-functional teams within an established process framework to deliver high-quality solutions, turning complex designs into reality. 

About Us

Dedicated to the world's tomorrow, Trimble is a technology company delivering solutions that enable our customers to work in new ways to measure, build, grow and move goods for a better quality of life. Core technologies in positioning, modeling, connectivity and data analytics connect the digital and physical worlds to improve productivity, quality, safety, transparency and sustainability. From purpose-built products and enterprise lifecycle solutions to industry cloud services, Trimble is transforming critical industries such as construction, geospatial, agriculture and transportation to power an interconnected world of work. For more information about Trimble (NASDAQ: TRMB), visit: www. trimble. com

Trimble Unity is a fully-integrated, owner and contractor-centric, cloud-based construction software focused exclusively on meeting the needs of facility owners and construction professionals. 

Trimble Unity Construct flagship product is an end-to-end Project Management Information Solution (PMIS) delivering outcomes from capital planning and design through commissioning. 

What Makes This Role Great

In this role, you will have a massive impact by driving the integration and performance of enterprise-level API services. You will seamlessly work across full-stack domains, leveraging your backend expertise while contributing to modern frontend workflows. Working from our Chennai office, you will have the autonomy to create software designs, participate in critical technical reviews, and collaborate directly with Product, QA, DevOps, and Architecture teams to deliver end-to-end global solutions. 

Key Exciting Responsibilities

- API Design & Development: Design, develop, and maintain RESTful APIs and microservices using industry best practices, ensuring adherence to secure coding standards and compliance guidelines. 
 - Full-Lifecycle Software Engineering: Create, implement, and test software designs within the process framework established by the Team to meet established requirements, maintaining up-to-date documentation (Swagger/OpenAPI). 
 - System Integration & Optimization: Integrate APIs with backend systems, databases (RDBMS and NoSQL), and third-party services while optimizing API performance, scalability, and security. 
 - Collaboration & Quality Assurance: Participate in technical/design reviews, provide constructive feedback in code reviews, and work independently or alongside quality assurance personnel to plan and execute comprehensive product testing. 
 - Operational Excellence: Troubleshoot and resolve API-related performance or functional issues, while handling other duties as required and requested by management. 

Essential Skills & Experience

- Professional Experience: 3-5 years of experience in software product development with a solid understanding of Object-Oriented Programming Concepts. 
 - Backend Mastery: Strong proficiency in API development and microservices-based architecture using Java / Spring Boot, Python / FastAPI / Flask, or . NET Core. Solid hands-on programming experience in Java developing high-quality, readable code. 
 - Frontend Development: Experience in UI development (React JS). 
 - Core API Concepts: Hands-on experience with REST APIs, JSON, OAuth2, JWT, and API gateways. 
 - Data & Environment: Strong knowledge of SQL/NoSQL databases and RDBMS, paired with a good working knowledge of Linux. 
 - CI/CD & Cloud Infrastructure: Experience with Git, continuous integration tools, cloud deployments, scripting, and familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP. 
 - Core Competencies: Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; a self-starter who is passionate about learning new technologies. 

Bonus Points For

- Advanced Integration Protocols: Experience with GraphQL and gRPC. 
 - Containerization & Operations: Knowledge of containerized applications (Docker, Kubernetes) and a solid understanding of DevOps practices. 
 - Observability & Tooling: Exposure to API monitoring tools (New Relic, Splunk, Postman, etc. ). 
 - Gateway Architecture: Experience with any one of the Gateway (AWS/Azure/WSO2/Apigee) functionalities. 
 - Mindset: A self-driven, go-getter attitude. 

Logistics

- Location: India - Chennai (In Office)
 - Job Level: Level P2
 - Job Type: Full-Time

Why You'll Love Working With Us

At Trimble, we're not just a company that "does good"-we are a team dedicated to making a tangible, positive Real-World Impact. We build innovative solutions designed to solve the world's most critical challenges. From construction sites to transportation hubs, our work tangibly improves how people live, build, move, and grow. 

- You'll work on projects that truly matter: Our purpose-driven culture means you'll be helping to build and deliver solutions that make work faster, safer, and more sustainable for millions of people worldwide. 
 - Collaborate with like-minded people: Our strong internal culture is a "hidden gem. " You will work with a collaborative, supportive team that shares your purpose and fosters a genuine sense of belonging. 
 - Be an owner: Trimble thrives on individuals who take initiative and embrace ownership. You'll find an entrepreneurial spirit where success is often "self-authored, " empowering proactive "doers. "
 - Enjoy true flexibility: We offer flexible work arrangements, which are a significant driver for employees joining and staying with us.

At Trimble, our core values of Belong, Grow, and Innovate aren't just words-they're the foundation of our culture. We foster an environment where you are seen, heard, and valued (Belong); where you have an opportunity to build a career and drive our collective growth (Grow); and where your innovative ideas shape the future (Innovate). data.title: Staff Digital Verification Engineer
data.description:
We Are

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 

You Are

You have spent years building verification environments that have to catch the bugs no one else saw coming, the corner cases that only show up when three protocols collide and a timing edge goes the wrong way. You know that a test plan is only as good as the bugs it finds, and you have learned to think like the design, like the system integrator, and like the customer all at once. 

You are the engineer who sees a coverage hole at 95% and knows exactly which scenario is missing. Writing assertions is not a checkbox exercise for you, it is how you encode your understanding of what should never happen. You have debugged enough waveforms to know when something smells wrong three layers deeper than the symptom. 

Leading a verification effort means more than running regressions. You set the strategy, you review the test plans your team writes, and you make the call on what gets verified to what depth. You work directly with RTL designers and architects, not to rubber-stamp their work but to push back when the intent is unclear or the interface is going to be painful to verify. 

At Synopsys, you will work on DesignWare IP that ships into real products. The verification environments you build will be used across product generations, and the bugs you catch will never make it to silicon. 

What You'll Be Doing

- Build and evolve SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments for DesignWare synthesizable IP cores, ensuring they scale across multiple product generations and configurations
 - Define comprehensive test plans that cover corner cases, protocol compliance, and system-level interactions for serial interface protocols and memory controllers, including DDR and LPDDR where applicable
 - Write and debug complex testbenches, checkers, and assertions that catch real bugs in critical PHY blocks and interface logic
 - Develop software requirements for the PHY that scale across various configurations and use cases
 - Own verification closure for multiple critical blocks within DDR PHYs, including functional coverage, code coverage, and formal signoff
 - Collaborate directly with RTL designers, digital architects, and circuit teams to align verification scope with design intent and surface issues early in the design cycle
 - Manage regression infrastructure and work with the infra team to optimize verification cycles, debug failures, and keep the environment reliable

The Impact You Will Have

- Your verification environments will catch critical bugs before tapeout, directly affecting the quality and time-to-market of DesignWare IP used across the semiconductor industry
 - The test plans you define and review will set the verification standard for the team, ensuring consistent coverage and reducing escapes
 - Your coverage-driven approach will surface gaps that others miss, leading to more robust IP and fewer silicon respins
 - The assertions and checkers you write will become reusable verification IP, accelerating future projects and raising the quality bar
 - Your collaboration with RTL and architecture teams will shape design decisions early, making designs easier to verify and more reliable in the field
 - The regression strategies you implement will directly improve team productivity and reduce verification cycle time
 - Your ownership of critical PHY blocks will ensure that high-stakes features meet functional and performance requirements on schedule

What You'll Need

- Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering or Electronics and Communication Engineering with 4+ years of hands-on verification experience
 - Proven track record leading verification teams through IP project delivery, including planning, execution, and signoff
 - Strong experience developing SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches from scratch and evolving them as designs grow in complexity
 - Deep expertise writing test plans, implementing checkers, and building assertions that catch real bugs, not just toggle coverage
 - Proficiency extracting and interpreting functional coverage and code coverage metrics, and using those insights to drive verification closure
 - Experience verifying serial interface protocols and working through IP design and verification processes, knowledge of DDR or LPDDR protocols is a strong plus
 - Demonstrated ability to own end-to-end verification deliverables, including metric closure and formal review signoff, experience with AI-assisted verification tools is a plus

Who You Are

- You can walk into a coverage review, spot the gap in the test plan, and articulate exactly what scenario is missing and why it matters
 - You write assertions that encode real design intent, not just the obvious cases, and you know the difference between a checker that catches bugs and one that just makes noise
 - You are comfortable leading technical discussions with RTL designers and architects, pushing back when verification scope is unclear or the interface is going to create downstream pain
 - You manage multiple verification efforts in parallel without losing track of what is at risk, what is on schedule, and what needs attention today
 - You debug with purpose, you do not just stare at waveforms hoping for insight, you form hypotheses, test them, and move systematically toward root cause
 - You treat verification infrastructure as a product, you care about regression efficiency, debug turnaround time, and whether your environment is actually usable by the rest of the team

The Team You'll Be Part Of

Your recruiter will share more about the team structure and mission during the interview process. 

Rewards and Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

data.title: Head of Injection Moulding (Mobile Industry)
data.description:
HEAD OF INJECTION MOULDING

Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech or Diploma - Plastics, Polymer, Mechanical or Production Engineering Mobile handset industry moulding experience is mandatory - please read below before applying

Moulding is where our product starts, and where our cost is set. A part moulded badly becomes a part printed badly, assembled badly and rejected at pack - by which point we've paid for all of it. 

You'd own moulding as a function: the floor, the process, the people, the capacity and the capital. That includes overmoulding - rigid shell with soft-touch elastomer - which is a meaningful part of what we produce and a materially harder process than single-shot. 

We are only considering candidates from the mobile handset industry

We want to be direct about this so nobody wastes their time. 

We make small, cosmetically critical parts - sub-millimetre wall sections, visible surfaces with no tolerance for sink or flow marks, tight fit against a device, and cosmetic standards closer to consumer electronics than to general plastics. A part that would pass in most moulding shops gets rejected here. 

The discipline that produces that output is learned in the handset supply chain, and it doesn't transfer quickly from elsewhere. Excellent moulding experience in automotive, appliance, packaging, housewares or general engineering plastics is genuinely excellent experience - it just isn't what this role needs, and we'd be setting you up to struggle. 

So: you should have spent meaningful time moulding handset housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures - at Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi, Realme, Transsion, Foxconn, Dixon, Lava or in their tier-one supplier base. Adjacent consumer electronics enclosure work at the same cosmetic standard will also be considered. 

The thing that actually limits this floor

We're high-mix. Many moulds, frequent changes, moderate volume per run. In that environment the constraint usually isn't cycle time - it's changeover and the scrap that follows it. Every tool change costs setup hours, then costs more shots before the process stabilises. Across a week of changes that's a serious share of capacity spent producing nothing. 

Most moulding operations measure cycle time obsessively and changeover barely at all. We'd like someone who goes after it. 

What you'd build

- Changeover discipline - SMED method, prepared tooling, parallel setup, and a measured changeover time that comes down
 - Validated parameter sets per mould, so a setter isn't rediscovering the process each time, and a first-off routine that reaches stable quickly and records what stable looked like
 - Material handling discipline - polymer dried to spec before it goes near a machine. Wet resin causes splay and cosmetic defects that get blamed on printing two stations later
 - A skill matrix for setters and operators, with certification before anyone runs unsupervised, and cross-training so capacity doesn't depend on one person's attendance
 - Real downtime and scrap data coded by cause, so improvement has something to aim at
 - Capacity planning and the case for new machines as we grow

You'd own

- Moulding production across shifts, against the plan
 - Scrap and first-pass yield at the machine. Your primary number
 - Process capability, parameter control and changeover performance
 - Machine utilisation, uptime and maintenance coordination
 - Tool condition in production - shot counts, preventive maintenance schedules, spare inserts and components, and escalation to the tool room before a tool fails rather than after
 - Tool repair and refurbishment decisions, with the cost case
 - Moulding capacity decisions and capital proposals
 - The moulding team - setters, operators, helpers, supervisors - including hiring and training
 - Safety, 5S and housekeeping

You need

- 12+ years in injection moulding, with function or plant-level ownership rather than shift supervision alone
 - Mobile handset moulding experience - mandatory. Housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures, at a handset OEM or in their tier-one supplier base. See the note above
 - Hands-on process capability. You can set a machine, read a short shot, and tell a setter what to change and why
 - Defect diagnosis: short shot, flash, sink, weld lines, warpage, splay, burn marks - cause, not just name
 - Material knowledge - PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, PP and filled grades; drying requirements, moisture sensitivity, masterbatch and regrind Overmoulding. A real part of our production and not a side skill: 
 - Two-shot and insert moulding - rotary platen, index and core-back methods, or mould-and-transfer. The machine and tool requirements of each, and when one suits better than the other
 - Material pairing and bond - which combinations bond chemically, which need mechanical interlock, and how melt temperature, shore hardness and surface condition affect adhesion. TPU and TPE over PC and PC/ABS specifically
 - Bond strength as an invisible defect. An overmoulded part can look perfect and delaminate weeks later in a customer's hand. It has to be designed and processed right, because inspection won't catch it. Peel and bond testing is part of the job, not an afterthought
 - Differential shrinkage and warpage between the two materials, and first-shot dimensional stability before the second shot
 - Cycle balancing - the slower shot sets the cycle, which makes process optimisation here a different problem from single-shot
 - Interface flash, colour bleed and the cosmetic defects specific to two-material parts

Tooling, in detail. This is not a nice-to-have for us: 

- Tool construction - mould base and insert construction, steel grades and hardness, cold and hot runner systems, gate types and vestige, cooling layout and what it does to cycle and warpage, venting, ejection, slides and lifters, shut-off surfaces, surface finish and texture
 - Two-shot tool construction - rotation and indexing, sealing at the material interface, second-shot shut-offs, and why these tools fail differently from single-shot ones
 - Tool condition on the floor - reading flash as parting line wear, galling on slides, blocked vents causing burns, scaled water lines quietly adding seconds to cycle, ejector wear, hot runner tip and heater faults. Catching these before they become a stoppage or a scrap run
 - Trials and correction - T0/T1/T2, reading trial results, steel-safe versus steel-removal corrections, shrinkage adjustment, and knowing when a correction is worth doing
 - Repair, refurbish or replace, with the judgement and the cost case behind each
 - The arbitration. The most valuable thing you'll do is decide whether a defect is a tool problem or a process problem. Process people blame the tool, tool rooms blame the process, and the part keeps failing while they argue. We want someone who settles it with evidence
 - Demonstrated changeover or scrap reduction with numbers. We'll ask for before and after
 - Team building across shifts, including developing setters
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: tool room or tool design background earlier in your career, scientific moulding or DOE training, multi-cavity and high-cavitation tooling, IMD/IML, take-out robots and automation, SMED implementation, CIPET background, OEE systems. 

Where this sits alongside our Tooling Engineer: they own mould design review and new tool development; you own tools in production - condition, maintenance, correction and when to retire them. You'll disagree occasionally, and that's healthy. 

Tell us: which handset programmes or customers you moulded for, your overmoulding experience and the material pairs you've run, your average changeover time and what you did to it, your scrap rate and how it was measured, one defect where you proved it was the tool and not the process (or the reverse) and how you proved it, and the cosmetic standard you worked to.

About Carrier

About The Role

- May propose changes in design or formulation to improve system and/or process reliability. 
 - Builds and conducts dry running of basic qualification test set ups. 
 - sCompiles and analyzes performance reports and process control statistics; investigates and analyzes relevant variables potentially affecting product performance and processes. 
 - Liaises closely with other project team members in the areas such as stress, manufacturing, sourcing and configuration, with respect to new designs or design changes. 

Key Responsibilities

Reliability Modeling & Prediction

- Perform reliability predictions for electronic assemblies and systems using industry-standard methodologies. 
 - Calculate: 
 - MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures)
 - Failure Rate (FIT)
 - Product Useful Life
 - Service Life Estimates
 - Reliability Growth Metrics
 - Reliability Block Diagrams (RBD)
 - Mission Reliability
 - Conduct reliability analysis using: 
 - Telcordia SR-332
 - MIL-HDBK-217F
 - IEC 61709
 - FIDES methodologies
 - Perform component-level and assembly-level reliability assessments
System-Level Reliability Analysis

- Develop and maintain system-level reliability models for complete products and platforms. 
 - Create reliability block diagrams - RBDs - for system architecture analysis. 
 - Evaluate reliability of complete systems considering: 
 - PCB assemblies
 - Sensors
 - Power supplies
 - Communication modules
 - Displays
 - Relays/contactors
 - Motors/fans
 - Connectors and harnesses
 - Mechanical/electromechanical interfaces
 - Analyze series, parallel, redundant, standby, and fail-safe architectures. 
 - Calculate system reliability, availability, maintainability, and probability of failure over mission time. 
 - Assess single-point failures and critical reliability contributors at system level. 
 - Support architecture trade-off studies to improve system robustness, redundancy, serviceability, and product life. 
 - Work with hardware, firmware, systems, mechanical, quality, compliance, and field teams to translate reliability risks into design actions
Product Lifetime & Wear-Out Analysis

- Estimate product useful life and service life based on operating profiles and field usage conditions.

 - Electrolytic capacitors
 - Relays
 - Power semiconductors
 - Fans
 - Connectors
 - Batteries
 - Displays
 - Electromechanical parts
 - Apply appropriate models such as Arrhenius, Weibull, Coffin-Manson, thermal acceleration, voltage derating, and duty-cycle-based life models. 
 - Evaluate environmental impact including temperature, humidity, vibration, cycling, load profile, and power-on hours. 
 - Recommend design margins, derating guidelines, and component selection improvements
Field Data Analytics

- Analyze warranty claims, field returns, service records, and customer failure data. 
 - Develop reliability dashboards and reliability KPIs. 
 - Identify dominant failure modes and reliability trends. 
 - Establish failure-rate distributions and reliability growth plans. 
 - Generate actionable recommendations to improve product robustness. 

Reliability Testing & Validation

- Define reliability validation plans for new product development and sustaining programs. 
 - Support HALT, HASS, accelerated life testing, temperature cycling, humidity testing, vibration testing, power cycling, and environmental stress testing. 
 - Correlate lab test results with predicted reliability and actual field performance. 
 - Define sample size, test duration, confidence level, and acceptance criteria for reliability demonstration tests. 
 - Support design verification and product qualification from a reliability perspective

Failure Analysis & Root Cause Investigation

- Support root cause investigations involving: 
 - Field failures
 - Manufacturing defects
 - Component failures
 - Early-life failures
 - Perform statistical analysis of failures. 
 - Work with hardware, firmware, component engineering, quality, manufacturing, and suppliers to implement corrective actions. 
Reliability Tools & Data Management

- Utilize reliability prediction software and databases for analysis and reporting. Expertise in Relex, Reliasoft, Minitab, ITEM tool suite

Experience - 3-5 years

Location - Vikhroli, Mumbai

CTC - 15-18 LPA

About the Role

We're looking for a Frontend Engineer to build and own product surfaces in NymbleUp's web app - the workforce-scheduling, LMS and video-analytics platform used daily by store managers and HR teams at large enterprise clients. You'll work in a Next. js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript codebase (App Router, MUI 7, Zustand, SCSS Modules) of roughly 250k lines, shipping features like the Workforce Scheduler: a virtualized week/day planner that stays interactive with 2, 000+ employee rosters, drag-and-drop shift editing, bulk actions and approval flows. This is a hands-on role for someone who cares about performance, state design and correctness in data-heavy UIs, not just pixel-pushing. 

What You'll Do

- Build and maintain features end-to-end in Next. js (App Router) and React 19 with TypeScript - route, view, store, service layer. 
 - Design client state with Zustand stores and selectors so that single edits don't re-render whole grids; keep server data flows clean through our Axios service layer and typed endpoint modules. 
 - Ship performance-sensitive UI: row virtualization, memoized cells, debounced filters, Web Workers for heavy rollups, and measured frame budgets on large rosters. 
 - Implement complex interactions - drag/resize/copy of shifts, keyboard editing, bulk apply, approval and publish flows - with correct date/time and timezone handling. 
 - Work with the Django backend team on API contracts: read responses critically, log blockers with concrete recommendations, never invent endpoints. 
 - Build with the shared component library and design tokens (MUI theme + SCSS tokens); extend it rather than re-rolling components. 
 - Debug production issues across multi-tenant deployments (auth/token refresh, tenant base-URL resolution, CSP, caching) and trace root causes. 
 - Take part in code reviews, keep typecheck/lint/build green, write clear PR descriptions, and help raise test coverage in a codebase that currently has none. 

Must-Have Qualifications

- B. E. /B. Tech in Computer Science (or equivalent CS engineering degree) - required. 
 - 3-5 years of professional frontend development, with at least 2 years in React + TypeScript on a production product. 
 - Strong React fundamentals: rendering model, memoization, hooks discipline, Server vs Client Components, and why a component re-renders. 
 - Hands-on Next. js App Router experience (layouts, route groups, server components, API/route handlers, middleware). 
 - Solid TypeScript - strict mode, generics, typed API layers, no `any` by habit. 
 - State management at scale (Zustand, Redux or similar) and data-fetching patterns with Axios/fetch, interceptors and token refresh. 
 - Comfort with CSS architecture: SCSS Modules, design tokens, responsive layouts, and a component library such as MUI. 
 - Strong debugging skills - browser DevTools, React Profiler, network traces; able to isolate and fix issues in a large codebase you didn't write. 
 - Strong analytical and logical reasoning - handles date/time, timezone and scheduling edge cases correctly and can defend design decisions. 

Good to Have

- Performance work on large lists/grids: @tanstack/react-virtual, Web Workers, canvas or similar. 
 - Drag-and-drop UIs (@hello-pangea/dnd, react-dnd), rich-text editors (TipTap), charts (Recharts), or data grids (AG Grid). 
 - Experience with multi-tenant SaaS, auth flows (JWT refresh rotation, OTP), CSP/security headers, and frontend VAPT fixes. 
 - Exposure to BFF/route-handler work in Next. js: third-party integrations (Zoho Desk, Google Maps/Sheets), rate limiting, streaming AI chat with the Vercel AI SDK. 
 - Testing: React Testing Library, Playwright or Vitest; helping set up a test culture from scratch. 
 - Node. js deployment basics (pm2, Cloudflare/OpenNext, CDN cache invalidation) and Git-based review workflows with conventional commits. 

What We're Looking For (Mindset)

- A problem-solver who treats a flaky drag interaction or a 5-hour timezone drift as a puzzle, not a chore. 
 - Someone who reads existing patterns before inventing new ones, and asks why before how. 
 - Strong ownership - sees features through from design proposal to verified production behaviour. 
 - A clear communicator who can explain technical trade-offs to backend, product and design peers. 

To apply, share your resume along with a brief note on a performance or state-management problem you solved in a React app and how you approached it.

data.title: Head of Printing
data.description:
Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech - Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production

Printing is the step that makes our product ours. It's also where most of our quality risk sits, because a defect found at pack is a part we've already paid to mould. 

Your scope is everything that happens to a part after it leaves the tool: UV printing, dye-sublimation, cylindrical and bottle printing, coating, and assembly - through to a finished product ready to pack. 

We have shift managers running the floor, an engineer keeping machines healthy, and a specialist owning colour. What we don't have is anyone accountable for whether our decoration as a whole is good and getting better - or for deciding what we should be able to produce two years from now. 

This role is technical before it is managerial. If you can't stand at a press and tell us why the part in your hand failed, the rest of the job won't work. 

And a large share of the time, the answer isn't the press. Adhesion failures usually trace back to materials - mould release contamination on the part surface, a substrate whose surface energy was never going to accept ink without treatment, plasticiser migrating out of a TPU weeks after it shipped. We want someone who looks upstream before blaming the machine. 

Who owns what - read this

Several roles touch printing, and all of them sit under you: 

- You own the outcome - print and assembly quality, process capability, and what we can and can't produce
 - Operations Managers own daily throughput and dispatch on their shifts
 - The UV Printing Engineer owns machine condition, maintenance and uptime
 - The Colour Management Specialist owns profiles and colour standards

When a defect appears, the diagnosis crosses all four. You decide where it actually came from, what changes, and you're accountable if it comes back. 

What you'd build

- Validated recipes per product and substrate across every process, so output doesn't depend on who's on shift
 - A process capability baseline - what our defect rates actually are, by type and by process. Harder to establish than it sounds, and impossible to improve without
 - A qualification route for new substrates and products, so new product development gets a real answer on printability and assembly rather than an opinion
 - Technology strategy: which process suits which product, where current capability runs out, and what we invest in next
 - A capability roadmap that lets us say yes to work we currently have to decline

Building the team

We're scaling, and most of our operators arrive without print-specific skills. How you build capability matters as much as how you build process. 

- A skill matrix per process - who can set up, who can run, who can judge quality on UV, sublimation, cylindrical and assembly. Certification before anyone operates unsupervised
 - Cross-training as a capacity lever, not an HR nicety. In high-mix production, if one person can set up the bottle line then that line's availability equals their attendance. Depth on every process is how we stop losing days to one person's leave
 - Limit samples, so "acceptable" is a physical object an operator can hold rather than an opinion that shifts by shift. Most quality arguments on a print floor are really definition arguments
 - Train-the-trainer, so capability multiplies rather than routing through you
 - A progression path that gives a good operator a reason to stay beyond the next ₹2, 000 offer
 - The structure of the function itself as we grow - shift coverage, technical specialists, quality

You'd own

- UV flatbed, cylindrical and bottle printing, dye-sublimation, coating and assembly
 - Quality and first-pass yield across the whole post-moulding chain. The number this role is judged on
 - Capacity planning against the production plan
 - Capital decisions for new capacity, and the business cases behind them
 - Customer complaints through to root cause and corrective action
 - The function and its team: shift operations, machine engineering, colour

You need

Real technical depth across our processes. Specifically: 

- Dye-sublimation - transfer printing onto polyester and poly-coated substrates, heat press and 3D vacuum sublimation, and how time, temperature and pressure shift the final result
 - UV inkjet - flatbed printing, LED curing, primer and surface preparation, white ink and varnish layers, and adhesion that holds up weeks later rather than just at inspection
 - Cylindrical and bottle printing - rotary setup, chuck alignment, tapered and non-uniform profiles, maintaining head gap over a curved surface
 - Assembly - multi-part products, fit and tolerance, insert handling, and cosmetic damage prevention on finished parts

Materials - plastics. How substrate behaviour decides what decoration is possible: PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, TPE, PP, PMMA and filled grades. Surface energy and dyne level, and which plastics need corona, plasma or flame treatment before they'll accept anything. Heat deflection limits, which govern what can be sublimated without distorting the part. Mould release carryover, plasticiser migration, and the other upstream causes of a print that fails three weeks later. 

Materials - coatings. Hard coat, soft-touch and PU systems, UV-curable versus two-component thermal cure. Primer and adhesion promoter selection. Mix ratio, pot life and cure schedules for 2K systems. Order of operations - coating over print versus print over coating - and why that choice is rarely reversible. Coating defects: orange peel, fish eyes, pinholes, poor levelling. 

Testing. Cross-hatch adhesion, abrasion, chemical and sweat resistance, and accelerated ageing - enough to establish whether a finish actually holds rather than assuming it will. 

Plus: 

- An engineering degree. B. E. /B. Tech in Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production. Printing Technology and Polymer Engineering map most closely to this role; a CIPET background is directly relevant on the materials side
 - 12+ years in industrial or digital printing production, with genuine function ownership rather than supervision alone
 - Defect diagnosis you can demonstrate - separating machine, ink, substrate, file, operator and environment as causes rather than guessing
 - Colour management fundamentals, fluent enough to challenge the specialist who owns them
 - Quality improvement with numbers - a defect rate you reduced, and how
 - Equipment selection and commissioning, with capital accountability
 - Demonstrated team building - you've hired, structured and grown a production team, not just inherited one
 - A training system you built, with evidence it worked: skill matrices, certification, limit samples, or whatever you used
 - Leadership across shifts and across technical specialists who know their speciality better than you do
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: injection moulding exposure, coating line operation, metals and glass decoration, high-mix short-run environments, screen or pad printing, IMD/IML, drinkware or promotional product decoration. 

Tell us: one print defect you root-caused where the obvious answer turned out to be wrong, one adhesion or coating failure you traced to a material cause, one quality metric you moved with before and after numbers, one operator you developed into something more, and the specific processes, substrates and coatings you've personally run.

About SunInfra

SunInfra Energies Ltd is an integrated renewable energy platform serving commercial, industrial and institutional consumers. Our Develop, Build and Own model connects project development, EPC delivery and long-term asset ownership. 

Our portfolio spans rooftop and utility-scale solar EPC, open-access solar parks, captive and group captive projects, battery energy storage integration, and operations and maintenance. We are building a clean energy platform that enables consumers to transition towards round-the-clock renewable energy through integrated generation, storage and energy management solutions.

We are seeking an experienced leader to take overall responsibility for project execution and operations across SunInfra's portfolio. 

Working directly with the Founder & CEO, you will lead teams, strengthen execution systems and drive accountability for delivery timelines, project profitability, quality, safety, complete project closure and operating asset performance. 

Key responsibilities

- Lead project delivery: Oversee projects from award through engineering coordination, procurement, construction, testing, commissioning and client handover. 
 - Strengthen planning and execution: Establish project schedules, budgets, resource plans and milestones. Conduct portfolio reviews and site inspections, resolve bottlenecks and implement recovery plans. 
 - Own commercial performance: Control execution costs, protect project margins and monitor forecast completion costs. Coordinate milestone certification, billing and collection follow-up with clients and Finance. 
 - Manage contractors and suppliers: Oversee scope, productivity, measurements, variations, claims, reconciliations and final settlements. 
 - Ensure quality and safety: Enforce quality standards, inspection processes and safe working practices. Ensure defects, equipment damage and execution risks are promptly reported, investigated and resolved. 
 - Complete technical and commercial closure: Ensure punch-list completion, performance testing, approvals and handover documentation. Prepare detailed project-wise techno-commercial closure reports, obtain relevant departmental sign-offs and client acknowledgement, and drive resolution of all outstanding matters. 
 - Lead operations and asset performance: Oversee O&M and AMC delivery, preventive maintenance, response timelines, plant performance, operating costs, warranties, spares and site security. 
 - Build teams and systems: Develop project managers, construction teams, site engineers, coordinators and O&M teams. Establish clear responsibilities, SOPs, dashboards and review routines. 
 - Manage stakeholders: Work closely with clients, consultants, contractors, utilities and internal departments to resolve escalations and maintain clear communication. 
 - 
Candidate profile - essential requirements

- B. E. /B. Tech. in Electrical, Mechanical, Civil or a related engineering discipline. 
 - 10+ years of experience in EPC or infrastructure project execution and operations is mandatory, including at least five years in a leadership role. 
 - Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and geographically dispersed teams against agreed timelines, budgets and quality standards. 
 - Strong understanding of engineering and construction interfaces, EPC contracts, cost control, commissioning and project economics. 
 - Proven ability to manage contractors, resolve client issues and achieve complete technical and commercial closure. 
 - Strong communication skills in English, sound commercial judgement and a disciplined, proactive approach. 
 - Comfortable with project scheduling tools, Excel, ERP systems and management reporting. 
 - Willingness to work from Thane and travel regularly across project sites and company offices. 

Preferred experience

Experience in solar or renewable energy-including rooftop and ground-mounted projects, open-access parks, captive/group captive assets, BESS or O&M-is preferred. Experience building teams and systems within a growing EPC or infrastructure organisation will be valued. 

Why join SunInfra?

This role offers the opportunity to work directly with the Founder & CEO, shape the execution and operations organisation, and contribute across an integrated renewable energy portfolio.

Email your CV and a brief summary of projects handled, team size, responsibilities and key achievements to hr@suninfra. co. in.

data.description:
About Chubb

Chubb is a world leader in insurance. With operations in 54 countries and territories, Chubb provides commercial and personal property and casualty insurance, personal accident and supplemental health insurance, reinsurance and life insurance to a diverse group of clients. The company is defined by its extensive product and service offerings, broad distribution capabilities, exceptional financial strength and local operations globally. Parent company Chubb Limited is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: CB) and is a component of the S&P 500 index. Chubb employs approximately 40, 000 people worldwide. Additional information can be found at: www. chubb. com. 

About Chubb India

At Chubb India, we are on an exciting journey of digital transformation driven by a commitment to engineering excellence and analytics. We are proud to share that we have been officially certified as a Great Place to Work for the third consecutive year, a reflection of the culture at Chubb where we believe in fostering an environment where everyone can thrive, innovate, and grow. 

With a team of over 2500 talented professionals, we encourage a start-up mindset that promotes collaboration, diverse perspectives, and a solution-driven attitude. We are dedicated to building expertise in engineering, analytics, and automation, empowering our teams to excel in a dynamic digital landscape. 

We offer an environment where you will be part of an organization that is dedicated to solving real-world challenges in the insurance industry. Together, we will work to shape the future through innovation and continuous learning. 

Position Details

Job Title: FinLines & Cyber Technology Lead

Function / Department: Technology

Employment Type: Full-time

Location: Hyderabad / Bangalore

Reports To: NA CI Technology Leadership (matrix: Financial Lines & Cyber Lead, US)

Role Overview

We are looking for a FinLines & Cyber Technology Lead who combines deep insurance domain expertise in Financial Lines and Cyber products with strong technology leadership. This is a matrix leadership role, working closely with the Financial Lines and Cyber business lead in the US while embedded within the Chubb India GCC technology team. You will drive technology strategy, platform evolution, and digital capabilities for one of Chubb's most dynamic and fastest-growing insurance segments - spanning Directors & Officers, Errors & Omissions, Management Liability, Employment Practices, and Cyber insurance. This role requires you to be equally fluent in insurance concepts and technology decisions. 

Key Responsibilities

- Serve as the primary technology leader for Financial Lines and Cyber insurance products within the NA CI engineering organisation. 
 - Partner closely with the FL & Cyber business lead in the US to align technology strategy with product strategy, underwriting priorities, and market expansion plans. 
 - Drive platform roadmap for Financial Lines and Cyber: policy administration, underwriting, rating, and claims systems specific to specialty lines. 
 - Lead technology initiatives specific to Cyber insurance - exposure data platforms, threat intelligence integration, cyber risk quantification tooling, and incident response data workflows. 
 - Define and govern integrations between FL/Cyber platforms and the broader Chubb technology estate: reinsurance, finance, claims, and distribution. 
 - Leverage AI and advanced analytics to enhance underwriting decisioning, risk assessment, and claims triage for complex specialty lines - including AI-assisted exposure analysis and emerging risk modelling. 
 - Operate effectively in a matrix structure: influence without direct authority, align teams across US and India, and build trusted relationships with global business and technology stakeholders. 
 - Engage with global architecture, product, actuarial, and underwriting stakeholders to represent FL/Cyber technology needs in enterprise planning forums. 
 - Build and lead a focused team of platform engineers and domain analysts embedded in the FL/Cyber value stream.

Company Description Modutec Ready Panels Pvt Ltd designs and manufactures modular switchboard enclosure systems that simplify panel building for domestic and international markets. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Bengaluru, India, the company focuses on modular technology, standardized components, and flexible configurations to help panel builders streamline fabrication, assembly, and logistics. Its portfolio includes modular LV switchboard enclosures, bayable systems, outdoor and wall-mounted enclosures, and modular accessories. The MODDIS platform supports Form 3 and Form 4 configurations, backed by extensive type testing to IEC 61439 and IEC/TR 61641, with high performance ratings and global-standard protection. Modutec serves customers across Africa, Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, and offers technical support, training, documentation, and compliance guidance to panel builders, system integrators, consultants, and distribution partners. 

Role Description The Mechanical Design Manager is a full-time, on-site role based in the Greater Bengaluru Area, responsible for leading the mechanical design function for modular switchboard enclosure systems. This role oversees concept development, detailed design, and engineering documentation for enclosure products, ensuring compliance with relevant standards and performance requirements. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing a design team, reviewing and approving CAD models and drawings, coordinating with electrical engineering, production, supply chain, and quality teams, and supporting type testing and product validation activities. The Mechanical Design Manager will optimize designs for manufacturability, flat-pack logistics, and assembly efficiency, while driving continuous improvement in design processes, tools, and standards. The role also involves collaborating with sales and application engineering to provide technical support on enclosure selection, customization, and project-specific solutions. 

Qualifications

- Strong mechanical design and engineering skills, including proficiency in 3D CAD and 2D drafting tools (e. g. , SolidWorks, Inventor, AutoCAD) and familiarity with sheet metal and enclosure design.

Job Title: Analytics Lead - Data, AI & Automation

Experience: 5-8 years

About MARS Cosmetics: 

MARS Cosmetics is a globally recognized beauty brand that thrives on innovation, diversity, and empowering individuals through high-quality beauty solutions. Headquartered in New Delhi, MARS Cosmetics is committed to offering groundbreaking products that meet the ever-evolving needs of consumers worldwide. 

About the Role: 

We are looking for a technically strong, hands-on Analytics Lead to build MARS Cosmetics' data intelligence capabilities. 

You will be responsible for organising data across business systems, developing automated data pipelines, integrating AI tools and LLMs, and building Python-based systems that proactively generate actionable business insights. 

Our objective is to move beyond conventional dashboards towards AI-powered, automated and event-driven business intelligence. 

This is a hands-on engineering and analytics role, not a traditional reporting or dashboard management position. 

Key Responsibilities: 

1. Data Engineering & Architecture

- Integrate and consolidate data from ERP, marketplaces, Shopify, distributor systems, marketing platforms and internal applications. 
 - Design and maintain reliable data pipelines, databases and analytical data models. 
 - Establish data quality, consistency and governance standards. 
 - Build scalable infrastructure that makes business data easily accessible for analytics and AI applications. 2. AI & LLM Integration

- Integrate structured business data with AI tools and LLMs such as OpenAI, Claude and other models through APIs. 
 - Develop AI-powered analytical workflows that investigate business performance and generate meaningful insights. 
 - Build natural-language interfaces that allow business teams to query and analyse data. 
 - Evaluate and implement emerging AI tools to improve analytical capabilities. 3. Python Automation & Event-Driven Insights

- Develop Python and SQL-based scripts for automated data processing, analysis and reporting. 
 - Build systems that proactively detect anomalies, emerging trends and business opportunities. 
 - Automate root-cause investigations and generate actionable recommendations. 
 - Create event-driven alerts for situations such as declining SKU sales, unusual inventory movements, margin deterioration and changes in advertising performance. 
 - Deliver automated insights through email, Teams, dashboards and other business applications. 4. Business Intelligence & Analytics

- Develop analytical frameworks covering sales, profitability, marketing, inventory and operations. 
 - Define standardised KPIs and reusable analytical datasets across business functions. 
 - Collaborate with business teams to identify high-impact analytical problems and translate them into automated solutions. 
 - Build dashboards and reporting systems wherever necessary. 5. Technical Ownership & Leadership

- Independently design, code, deploy and maintain analytical systems. 
 - Establish best practices for testing, monitoring, documentation and security. 
 - Lead and mentor a lean team of data and analytics engineers. 
 - Prioritise initiatives based on business impact, scalability and execution speed. Required Skills: 

- Python: Advanced proficiency in Pandas, data processing, scripting, automation and API integrations. 
 - SQL & Databases: Strong SQL skills, data modelling and experience with relational databases or data warehouses. 
 - Data Engineering: Experience building ETL/ELT pipelines and integrating multiple data sources. 
 - AI/LLMs: Hands-on experience with LLM APIs, function calling, AI agents or AI-powered analytical workflows. 
 - Analytics: Strong statistical reasoning, anomaly detection and business problem-solving capabilities. 
 - Automation: Experience developing scheduled and event-driven workflows. 
 - Engineering: Experience deploying, monitoring and maintaining production-grade solutions. Good to Have: Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, dbt, workflow orchestration tools, and experience in e-commerce, FMCG or retail. 

Ideal Candidate: 

- A hands-on builder, not just a dashboard developer or analytics manager. 
 - Has independently built end-to-end data and analytical systems. 
 - Strong in both technical engineering and commercial problem-solving. 
 - Comfortable working with fragmented data and converting it into reliable, actionable intelligence. 
 - Curious, resourceful and capable of independently evaluating new tools and technologies. 
 - Demonstrates ownership, speed of execution and a preference for simple, scalable solutions. What Success Looks Like: 

Within the first 90 days, you should have: 

- Established reliable data pipelines and structured datasets for priority business functions. 
 - Developed automated systems to detect significant business anomalies and opportunities. 
 - Integrated analytical workflows with LLMs to generate evidence-backed insights. 
 - Deployed at least two automated intelligence workflows delivering actionable insights to business stakeholders. Why Join MARS?

- Opportunity to build an AI-native analytics function from the ground up. 
 - Work directly on high-impact business problems across multiple functions. 
 - Significant technical ownership and freedom to evaluate modern technologies. 
 - Build intelligent systems that influence real business decisions.

You will combine deep AI expertise with strong software and security engineering judgment. You will guide the team in selecting the right problems for AI, validating solutions against rigorous quality and safety standards, and operating them effectively at cloud scale. 

- Set the technical strategy and architecture for applied AI in ETD, connecting customer problems and product goals to a clear engineering roadmap.

 - Lead resolution of complex customer-impacting issues and ensure production readiness through observability, incident response, root-cause analysis, and operational follow-through.

data.title: DevOps and MLOps Engineer
data.description:
Hyperworks Imaging is a cutting-edge technology company based out of Bengaluru, India since 2016. We are seeking an ambitious junior ML researcher who wants to do more than fine-tune off-the-shelf models. In this role, you will build, train and deploy new LLMs, SLMs, VLMs and AI agents from the ground up - designing architectures, running training experiments, and shipping models into production systems that power the AI assistants of the future. 

We are seeking a high-ownership DevOps & MLOps Engineer with 2-3 years of hands-on experience to own and manage our hybrid cloud infrastructure across Azure (Primary Preference) and AWS (Secondary). In this role, you will be responsible for multi-environment cloud provisioning (Dev, Staging, Production), automated wildcard subdomain routing, API Gateways, centralized logging stacks, database reliability, cloud cost governance, and text-to-speech (TTS) AI pipelines across multiple internal applications. 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Cloud Infrastructure & Automation (IaC)

- Manage secure multi-environment (Dev/Staging/Prod) provisioning on Azure and AWS using Terraform modules. 
 - Standardize container build workflows and infrastructure state management. 2. Networking, Subdomain Routing & Gateways

- Automate wildcard subdomains, CNAME mappings, and ingress routing. 
 - Manage API Gateways (Azure APIM, AWS API Gateway, NGINX, Traefik, Kong). 
 - Handle SSL/TLS lifecycles via Cloudflare, Azure Key Vault, or AWS ACM. 3. AI, Speech & Storage Pipelines

- Maintain low-latency TTS integration pipelines (AWS Polly, Azure Speech Services). 
 - Optimize AWS S3/Azure Blob Storage lifecycle rules, access controls, and CDN delivery. 4. Database Administration & Performance

- Manage, tune, and scale PostgreSQL and Redis databases. 
 - Configure PgBouncer, read-replicas, automated snapshots, and point-in-time recovery. 5. Cost Governance & Observability

- Audit/optimize Azure/AWS spending (Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, rightsizing). 
 - Maintain centralized logging (ELK, Loki, CloudWatch) and metrics dashboards (Prometheus, Grafana). 6. Security, CI/CD & MLOps

- Enforce Zero-Trust IAM, secrets management (Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager), and OAuth/JWT auth. 
 - Manage CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps) for Node. js/Python microservices. 
 - Deploy ML inference endpoints (MLflow, BentoML, SageMaker, Azure ML). 

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

- Experience Level: 2-3 Years
 - Educational Requirement: B. Tech / B. E. / B. S. in Computer Science, IT, or related technical field

Must Have Skills: 

- Experience: 2-3 years of proven hands-on experience in DevOps, Cloud Platform, or Systems Engineering in a fast-paced environment. 
 - Hybrid Cloud: Direct experience managing workloads on AWS (Primary) and exposure to Azure as well. 
 - Infrastructure as Code: High proficiency in writing declarative, modular Terraform code. 
 - Database Management: Practical experience with PostgreSQL and Redis administration, query tuning, and automated backup strategies. 
 - Networking & Gateways: Hands-on setup of API Gateways, wildcard DNS routing, and SSL certificate management. 
 - Audio & Cloud Storage: Experience integrating cloud Speech/TTS APIs (AWS Polly / Azure Speech) and handling cloud object storage (S3 / Azure Blob). 
 - Cost Optimization: Demonstrated track record of auditing and reducing cloud expenditure across AWS or Azure. 
 - Logging & Monitoring: Setup and management of centralized logging (Loki, ELK, or CloudWatch) and metrics collection (Prometheus + Grafana). 
 - Containers & CI/CD: Hands-on expertise with Docker and automated pipeline creation via GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps. 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (Nice-To-Have)

- Certifications: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate, or HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate. 
 - MLOps Frameworks: Prior exposure to model deployment frameworks (MLflow, BentoML, TorchServe, Azure ML, or AWS SageMaker). 
 - Backend Debugging: Ability to read and debug Node. js or Python backend code. Please note that we will reach out to ONLY those applicants who satisfy the criteria listed above. 

SALARY DETAILS: commensurate with experience

JOINING DATE: Immediate

JOB TYPE: full time

CONTACT: naveen@hyperworksimaging. com

data.title: Chief Cloud Infrastructure & Security Officer
data.description:
Job Description

Senior Director / Vice President, Cloud Operations & Security Engineering

Location: Chennai DLF

Employment type: Full-time

Experience: 20+ years

Role Summary

Talentgigs is seeking an experienced technology leader to own and advance Production Operations, Cloud Infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevSecOps, and Security Engineering. 

This leader will bring deep technical judgment and a strong record of leading cloud-native production environments. They will build a capable, accountable organization that protects and operates critical services through reliable engineering, proactive security, automation, continuous monitoring, and disciplined incident management. 

The role extends beyond traditional infrastructure management and information security management system (ISMS) compliance. The successful candidate will embed security and reliability in engineering and operational practices, reduce risk before it becomes an incident, and use automation and AI-driven operations to improve service health and response. 

Key Responsibilities

Production Operations and Reliability

- Own the reliability, availability, performance, and operational readiness of production services. 
 - Establish clear service ownership, operational accountability, escalation paths, and on-call practices. 
 - Lead incident response, service restoration, root-cause analysis, and follow-through on corrective actions. 
 - Define and improve service-level objectives, service-level indicators, error budgets, and operational health measures. 
 - Strengthen change, release, capacity, resilience, backup, and disaster-recovery practices. 
 - Reduce recurring incidents and operational toil through engineering-led improvements. Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Engineering

- Set the direction for secure, scalable, resilient, and cost-aware cloud infrastructure. 
 - Lead the design and operation of cloud-native platforms, environments, networks, identity controls, and shared services. 
 - Promote infrastructure as code, standard platform patterns, self-service capabilities, and repeatable environment provisioning. 
 - Ensure platform design supports availability, recovery, observability, performance, and secure delivery. 
 - Guide capacity planning, cloud cost visibility, and optimization without compromising reliability or security. SRE and Operational Excellence

- Build and mature SRE practices that make reliability measurable and part of day-to-day engineering. 
 - Develop observability across services using actionable metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and service health views. 
 - Improve deployment safety through progressive delivery, automated checks, rollback readiness, and resilient release practices. 
 - Use incident trends, operational data, and post-incident reviews to guide prioritized improvements. 
 - Create a culture of learning and accountability in which incidents lead to durable fixes. DevSecOps and Security Engineering

- Embed security into software delivery, infrastructure management, and operational workflows. 
 - Lead practical security engineering across identity and access, secrets, configuration, network controls, workload protection, and data safeguards. 
 - Build automated security checks into build, test, deployment, and infrastructure pipelines. 
 - Establish continuous monitoring and threat detection with clear triage, escalation, and response ownership. 
 - Drive vulnerability prevention and remediation through asset visibility, risk-based prioritization, patching, secure configuration, and dependency controls. 
 - Strengthen cloud security posture and address risks across applications, platforms, identities, and operational processes. 
 - Partner with product and engineering teams to resolve security issues early and sustainably. 
 - Ensure audits and ISMS obligations are supported by effective technical controls and evidence, while keeping operational security and risk reduction at the center. Automation and AI-Driven Operations

- Set an automation strategy that reduces manual work, improves consistency, and speeds up safe delivery and recovery. 
 - Apply AI and advanced analytics to suitable operational use cases, such as anomaly detection, alert correlation, incident triage, capacity forecasting, and knowledge retrieval. 
 - Establish appropriate safeguards, human oversight, validation, and access controls for AI-supported operational workflows. 
 - Measure automation outcomes through reduced toil, faster response, fewer repeat incidents, and improved service health. Organization and Leadership

- Build, develop, and retain strong teams across production operations, cloud infrastructure, SRE, DevSecOps, and security engineering. 
 - Define organizational structure, role clarity, decision rights, service ownership, and measurable accountability. 
 - Develop senior technical leaders and create growth paths for engineering and operations talent. 
 - Work closely with product, application engineering, architecture, risk, and business leaders to align technology priorities with business outcomes. 
 - Communicate operational risk, service health, security posture, and investment needs clearly to executive stakeholders. 
 - Lead through technical credibility, sound judgment, collaboration, and consistent follow-through. Required Technical Qualifications

- 20+ years of progressive experience in technology, infrastructure, production operations, cloud engineering, reliability, or security, including substantial leadership responsibility. 
 - Demonstrated hands-on technical leadership in cloud-native production environments. 
 - Strong understanding of cloud architecture, distributed systems, networking, identity, compute, storage, and platform operations. 
 - Experience designing and operating containerized and orchestrated workloads, such as Kubernetes or comparable platforms. 
 - Practical knowledge of infrastructure as code, configuration management, CI/CD, source control, and deployment automation. 
 - Deep working understanding of SRE principles, observability, service-level objectives, incident management, resilience, and disaster recovery. 
 - Experience implementing security controls in cloud and software delivery environments, including identity management, secrets, vulnerability management, secure configuration, and threat detection. 
 - Experience establishing continuous monitoring, alerting, incident response, and security operations practices. 
 - Ability to assess architecture and operational risk, make trade-offs, and guide teams through complex technical decisions. 
 - Familiarity with cloud cost management and capacity planning in production environments. Required Leadership Qualifications

- Experience leading multiple technical functions and managing managers or senior technical leaders. 
 - Track record of building technically strong teams with clear ownership and measurable outcomes. 
 - Ability to stay close to technical decisions while setting direction and enabling teams to execute. 
 - Proven leadership in major incidents, security events, operational change, or complex service transformations. 
 - Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risk and investment priorities to executive and non-technical audiences. 
 - A practical, engineering-led approach to governance, risk management, and compliance. 
 - Demonstrated ability to build trust and work across organizational boundaries. Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience leading operations and security in a high-scale, high-availability, or business-critical environment. 
 - Experience modernizing legacy infrastructure and operational models into cloud-native platforms and practices. 
 - Familiarity with zero-trust principles, security architecture, threat modeling, and secure software supply chains. 
 - Experience with chaos engineering, resilience testing, game days, and recovery exercises. 
 - Experience using AI or machine learning to improve operational monitoring, incident workflows, or engineering productivity. 
 - Familiarity with security and service-management frameworks or standards relevant to the organization. 
 - Relevant cloud, security, SRE, or leadership certifications. Success Measures

Success in this role will be assessed through sustained improvements in: 

- Production service availability, reliability, performance, and recovery readiness. 
 - Incident frequency, severity, time to detect, time to restore, and recurrence rates. 
 - Adoption and quality of service-level objectives, observability, and service ownership. 
 - Vulnerability exposure, remediation timelines, secure configuration, and cloud security posture. 
 - Security monitoring coverage, alert quality, response readiness, and closure of corrective actions. 
 - Automation coverage, reduction in manual toil, and safe deployment frequency. 
 - Resilience, backup, disaster-recovery, and continuity test outcomes. 
 - Cloud cost visibility and efficiency while meeting reliability and security requirements. 
 - Team capability, role clarity, leadership depth, and accountability across the functions. 
 - The ability of engineering teams to adopt secure and reliable practices as part of normal delivery.

data.title: Engineer II, Systems
data.description:
This is where your work makes a difference. 

At Baxter, we believe every person-regardless of who they are or where they are from-deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond. 

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results. 

Here, you will find more than just a job-you will find purpose and pride. 

Your Role At Baxter

The role of Engineer II , Product Owner is to contribute in design and development of a product or solution, from conception to design and verification/validation. You will apply expert technical knowledge and engineering principles in the development of products and solutions. You will collaborate with cross functional team for technical issues, design changes, design reviews, and complex problem resolution

What You'll Be Doing

- Define and translate customer, business, regulatory, performance, usability, and safety requirements into clear system requirements and product specifications. 
 - Lead requirements engineering activities, including use case development, requirements decomposition, traceability, and change management using tools such as DOORS, Polarion, or equivalent platforms. 
 - Apply systems engineering principles to balance design trade-offs, identify risks early, and support informed technical decision-making. 
 - Execute and support risk management activities in accordance with ISO 14971, ensuring product safety and regulatory compliance throughout the development lifecycle. 
 - Partner with cross-functional engineering teams to resolve technical challenges and drive optimal technology solutions. 
 - Support Usability Engineering and Human Factors activities, ensuring compliance with IEC 62366 and relevant FDA guidance. 
 - Apply reliability and robustness engineering principles to enhance product performance, quality, and customer experience. 
 - Develop high-quality technical documentation that effectively communicates system architecture, requirements, design decisions, and development outcomes. 
 - Collaborate closely with software, hardware, and systems teams to support successful product integration and development testing. 
 - Work with Verification & Validation (V&V) teams to define comprehensive verification strategies and test plans that ensure thorough requirements coverage. 
 - Provide technical leadership and expertise to help projects achieve key objectives related to quality, cost, schedule, and regulatory compliance. 
 - Contribute to the successful delivery of innovative healthcare solutions by championing best practices in systems engineering, risk management, and product development. 

What You'll Bring

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline. 
 - 3-6 years of experience in Systems Engineering, with a strong focus on electro-mechanical product development. 
 - Experience supporting the development of complex products within highly regulated industries, preferably medical devices. 
 - Working knowledge of FDA regulations, Medical Device Regulation (MDR), and applicable quality and regulatory standards. 
 - Experience with requirements management, systems engineering processes, and product lifecycle development. 
 - Familiarity with Usability Engineering and Human Factors Engineering methodologies. 
 - Understanding of design and development tools and methodologies such as QFD (Quality Function Deployment), Pugh Matrix, CTQ (Critical to Quality), Design for Reliability (DFR), and Design for Excellence (DFX). 
 - Knowledge of FDA, ISO, and IEC standards, including design controls, risk management, and product development best practices. 
 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate complex technical challenges and recommend effective solutions. 
 - Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and successfully deliver project objectives within quality, cost, and schedule expectations. 
 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams. 

Equal Employment Opportunity

Baxter is an equal opportunity employer. Baxter evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic. 

Reasonable Accommodations

Baxter is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities globally. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please click on the link here and let us know the nature of your request along with your contact information. 

Recruitment Fraud Notice

Baxter has discovered incidents of employment scams, where fraudulent parties pose as Baxter employees, recruiters, or other agents, and engage with online job seekers in an attempt to steal personal and/or financial information. To learn how you can protect yourself, review our Recruitment Fraud Notice.

data.title: QA Automation Engineer – Python + Playwright
data.description:
About the RoleWe're looking for a QA Automation Engineer to own the quality of our web product. You'll build and maintain our automated test suite using Playwright and Python, and you'll work closely with developers and product to catch issues early and ship with confidence. We care about automation, but we also want someone with a good instinct for exploratory testing and for knowing what's worth automating. 

What You'll Do•        Design, build, and maintain end-to-end UI test suites using Playwright with Python and pytest, and keep them fast, parallel, and reliable. 

•        Write automated API tests for REST services with Playwright's API testing or Python libraries like requests or httpx. 

•        Investigate failures and fix flaky tests, using Playwright traces, screenshots, and logs to get to the root cause. 

•        Write test plans and test cases for new features, and do exploratory and manual testing where automation isn't the right tool. 

•        Run regression, smoke, and cross-browser testing (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) before releases. 

•        File clear, reproducible bug reports and work with developers to verify fixes. 

•        Review requirements and designs early to flag testability issues and edge cases. 

•        Help shape our overall test strategy, coverage, and quality metrics. 

Must-Haves•        [3+] years of QA experience, with at least [2] years in test automation. 

•        Strong Python skills: you write clean, maintainable, reusable test code, not just scripts that happen to pass. 

•        Hands-on Playwright experience (Python), including locators, auto-waiting, fixtures, authentication/storage state, network interception, and tracing. 

•        Solid experience with pytest: fixtures, parametrization, markers, and plugins. 

•        Experience with the Page Object Model or similar patterns for structuring test frameworks. 

•        Strong testing fundamentals: test design techniques (boundary values, equivalence partitioning), the bug lifecycle, and the difference between smoke, sanity, and regression testing. 

•        Experience testing REST APIs. 

•        Comfortable with Git. 

•        Experience with a bug tracker like Jira or Linear. 

•        Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a bug so a developer can reproduce it on the first try. 

Nice to Have•        Experience with Docker and running tests in containers. 

•        Basic SQL for test data setup and validation. 

•        Performance testing (Locust, k6, or JMeter). 

•        Accessibility or visual regression testing. 

•        Cloud testing platforms like BrowserStack or LambdaTest.
